findings.text: The report correctly shows that agent lane constructs http://{endpoints[0].host}:{port}, but then concludes that binding the engine to loopback leaves that dial working merely because the refresher runs on the same node. A socket bound only to loopback does not accept traffic addressed to the node's FQDN/non-loopback interface. With the currently published 98dci4-gpu-0003.iter.org:18810 origin, the refresher would stop updating lane.json after the bind unless its explicit origin or the document contract is changed. Therefore the claims that the bind alone needs no consumer/document change and that agent lane survives it are unsafe deployment guidance.

The manifest records outcome summaries for the three-document selection but names the generated launcher, an empty diff and the rendered launcher as test logs; none is a revision/tree/command-headed result receipt, and no named file records the three selected origins or curl exits. The stream preserves contemporaneous execution, but the declared test_logs do not let a later reader verify the quantitative result directly.
